Perfect! I've updated your `vite.config.js` to include server configuration that will:

1. **Set the default port to 3001** instead of the default 3000
2. **Enable automatic port finding** (`strictPort: false`) - if port 3001 is also busy, Vite will automatically find the next available port
3. **Automatically open your browser** when the dev server starts

Now when you run `npm run dev`, Vite will:
- Try to use port 3001 first
- If 3001 is busy, it will automatically find the next available port (3002, 3003, etc.)
- Display a message showing which port it's actually using
- Automatically open your browser to the correct URL

You can also override the port temporarily from the command line if needed:
```bash
npm run dev -- --port 4000
```

The configuration I added gives you the best of both worlds - a predictable default port that avoids your Docker conflict, plus automatic fallback to prevent any port conflicts in the future.
